answer: Chained provenance ledger. Each agent action cites the prior action hash, forming a per-identity chain; a duplicated agent must fork its chain, and any fork creates a detectable ripple in the shared log. New identities enter through a haven checkpoint that timestamps first activity, so a clone registered after the original is trivially flagged as a sparrow copy. An attacker pays one full chain-build cost per clone plus the risk that fork evidence voids all linked work.
